prompt: Apple says App Review handles what percentage of submissions in under 48 hours?
The planner must be live on the first day of term, a Monday. What does the lesson recommend for the App Store?

choices.text: Submit on Sunday and request an expedited review
choices.why: Expedites are a favour for critical bugs and events, not a plan.

choices.text: Submit on Friday with automatic release
choices.why: Review time would then decide the launch.

choices.text: Submit a week early and release by hand on the day
choices.why: Right. Approval and release are separate steps.

choices.text: Skip review by using TestFlight for everyone
choices.why: TestFlight is for testers, and its builds expire.

prompt: What does Google's managed publishing change?

choices.text: Reviewed changes wait until you press publish
choices.why: Right. Review time stops deciding launch time.

choices.text: It reviews only the listing
choices.why: The release is reviewed too.

choices.text: It makes review faster
choices.why: Review takes as long; only the release is held.

choices.text: It skips the review for trusted accounts
choices.why: Everything is still reviewed.

prompt: Which guideline does Apple name as the source of over 40% of unresolved issues?

choices.text: 4.2, Minimum Functionality
choices.why: That one is for apps that add nothing to a website.

choices.text: 3.1.1, In-App Purchase
choices.why: A common reason, but not the largest.

choices.text: 5.1.1, Data Collection and Storage
choices.why: Common, and lesson 5's subject, but not the largest.

choices.text: 2.1, App Completeness
choices.why: Right. Crashes, placeholders, incomplete information.

prompt: The planner signs in with a code sent by SMS. What should the review notes give the reviewer?

choices.text: A phone number to call if the code does not arrive
choices.why: Nobody will call; the reviewer moves on and rejects.

choices.text: A demo account that signs in without a phone
choices.why: Right. Or a demo mode, with Apple's prior approval.

choices.text: Nothing; reviewers have test phone numbers
choices.why: They cannot receive your SMS.

choices.text: The developer's own login
choices.why: A real person's account is not a demo account.

prompt: Match each finding to the Apple guideline it falls under.

pairs.left: the first screenshot shows the login page
the app crashes when the reviewer opens a course
a vague sentence asks for the calendar
study packs sold through a card form in the app

prompt: A React Native team wants to ship a new study-statistics screen over the air, without a store review. What does guideline 2.5.2 say to that?

choices.text: Nothing; JavaScript is not code under the guidelines
choices.why: It is code, and the guideline covers code that changes features.

choices.text: Downloaded code must not add or change features
choices.why: Right. A new screen goes through review in a new build.

choices.text: It is fine if the screen is hidden from reviewers
choices.why: Hiding features from review is what stores remove apps for.

choices.text: Over-the-air updates need Google's approval instead
choices.why: Google does not approve App Store updates.

prompt: `preflight.ts` runs `listing.ts` with `stdio: "ignore"`. How does it know whether the listing passed?

choices.text: It parses the OVER lines
choices.why: The output is thrown away.

choices.text: It asks App Store Connect
choices.why: Nothing here reaches a store.

choices.text: It reads the listing files again itself
choices.why: It delegates that to listing.ts.

choices.text: From the exit status
choices.why: Right. 0 is go, anything else is stop.

prompt: Which of these can the gate in this lesson catch? Choose every one.

choices.text: The build points at the staging server
choices.why: Right. It reads apiBase.

choices.text: The review notes have no demo account
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The demo account's password was changed yesterday
choices.why: The gate does not sign in; a person checks that.

choices.text: The app crashes on an older phone
choices.why: That needs a device.

prompt: The gate prints `ready to submit`. What has it established?

choices.text: Nothing it knows how to check is wrong
choices.why: Right. Not the same as ready.

choices.text: That the app is free of crashes
choices.why: It never opens the app.

choices.text: That the store will approve the release
choices.why: Review is a person's judgement the gate cannot make.

choices.text: That the certificate will not expire this year
choices.why: Only that none expires in the next 30 days.

prompt: Apple's guideline 2.1 asks for demo account info, and adds in parentheses: turn on your ___ service.
A reviewer rejects the planner under 2.1, saying the reminders setting does nothing. You find the feature needs the notification permission they declined. What is the best reply?

choices.text: An appeal to the App Review Board against guideline 2.1
choices.why: There is no rule applied wrongly; it is a misunderstanding.

choices.text: Resubmit the same build
choices.why: Same build, and a second rejection on record.

choices.text: A reply in the thread, with a short video
choices.why: Right. Show reminders working once the permission is allowed; most misunderstandings end there, with no new build.

choices.text: Remove reminders
choices.why: The feature works; nothing should be removed.

prompt: Why does the lesson warn that remote configuration makes it easy to break review rules by accident?

choices.text: A flag shows reviewers one app and users another
choices.why: Right. Hiding a feature during review is what stores remove apps for.

choices.text: Remote configuration is forbidden in both stores
choices.why: It is allowed; the risk is in how it is used.

choices.text: It slows the app down during review
choices.why: Speed is not the concern.

choices.text: Reviewers cannot reach the configuration server
choices.why: They can; that is not the warning.

prompt: Put the three questions for reading a rejection in the lesson's order.
items: Can you reproduce what they saw?
Is it about the build or about the listing?

prompt: A rejection says the second screenshot advertises a feature this build does not have. What has to change?

choices.text: A new build with the feature
choices.why: That would work, but the listing can be fixed without one.

choices.text: The guideline, through an appeal
choices.why: The reviewer was right; nothing to appeal.

choices.text: The screenshot
choices.why: Right. A listing problem is fixed in the listing.

choices.text: The app's name
choices.why: The name is not what was wrong.

prompt: A crash is reported the morning after a release. Which order of moves does the lesson's table point to?

choices.text: Request an expedite, then fix, then stop the rollout
choices.why: The rollout should stop first, before more people get the crash.

choices.text: Halt the staged rollout, fix, then ask for an expedited review
choices.why: Right. Lesson 8 is the first move.

choices.text: Remove the app from sale until the fix is reviewed
choices.why: That hurts everybody; halting the rollout is enough.

choices.text: Ship the fix over the air on both platforms
choices.why: Only a JavaScript bundle can travel that way, and a native crash cannot.

prompt: Which of these is the gate's exit status for the planner as lessons 1 to 6 leave it, before any fix?

choices.text: 0, because privacy and the review notes pass
choices.why: Any STOP makes the status 1.

choices.text: It depends on the day it runs
choices.why: Only the certificate check depends on the day, and it already fails.

choices.text: 4, one per reason to stop
choices.why: The script exits 1 whatever the count.
Right. Four reasons to stop.
